requirements.text: identify all her active cases, assign them to Lisa Smith, and make sure those cases are now owned by the Case Assignment_3 support group
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id IN (251, 1142) AND assigned_to = 496 AND assignment_group_id = 44
requirements.source: All Active Tabitha Cases Reassigned To Lisa
assumptions: Tabitha Bullock is user 3 and Lisa Smith user 496 (agent, active), each the only user of that name; Case Assignment_3 is group 44, the exact name match
active cases are those not resolved, closed or canceled: of user 3's three cases, 251 (new) and 1142 (in_progress) are active and 1088 (canceled) is not
state not stated; neither request nor policy fixes it, so it is not tested

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1088 AND assigned_to = 3 AND assignment_group_id = 67
assumptions: case 1088 is also assigned to Tabitha but canceled, so it is outside her active cases and keeps its assignment; reassigning it would sweep in a case the request leaves out

requirements.text: assign them to Lisa Smith, and make sure those cases are now owned by the Case Assignment_3 support group
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE member_id = 960 AND group_id = 44 AND user_id = 496
requirements.source: Lisa Is Member Of Case Assignment_3
assumptions: implied by the request, not stated: the policy requires assigned_to to be a member of the assignment group, and user 496 is in groups 9 and 63 only on the seed
id assumed next in sequence (highest member_id on the seed is 959)

requirements.text: owned by the Case Assignment_3 support group
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE user_id = 496 AND group_id IN (4, 24, 64)
assumptions: groups 4, 24 and 64 are Case Assignment, Case Assignment_2 and Case Assignment_4, near matches of the named group; Lisa is not added to them

requirements.text: After the reassignment is complete, offboard Tabitha's profile
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "user" WHERE user_id = 3 AND first_name = 'Tabitha' AND last_name = 'Bullock' AND active = 0
assumptions: offboarding the profile means deactivating user 3 (active = 0), active on the seed; the request asks for no role or other profile change

requirements.text: send a report notification to their contact confirming that a new case owner has been assigned
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE case_id = 251 AND email = 'brandon.davis@vehementcap.com' AND type = 'report' AND status = 'success'
assumptions: case 251's contact is contact 15, Brandon Davis (user 10, brandon.davis@vehementcap.com) of Vehement Capital Partners
two notifications are created, so each is selected by its case and recipient, not by id
the benchmark check reaches the recipient through the case's contact; the requirement tests the notification's own email, since the request sends it to the case's contact
status success kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy

requirements.text: send a report notification to their contact confirming that a new case owner has been assigned
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE case_id = 1142 AND email = 'david.trujillo@hernandezbarnettandstewart.com' AND type = 'report' AND status = 'success'
assumptions: case 1142's contact is contact 112, David Trujillo (user 340, david.trujillo@hernandezbarnettandstewart.com) of Hernandez, Barnett and Stewart
the request's singular 'the customer whose active case' is read as each customer with an active case, since both active cases are reassigned
two notifications are created, so each is selected by its case and recipient, not by id
the seed already holds an update notification (681) to this address for case 1142; the type report keeps it out of the count
the benchmark check reaches the recipient through the case's contact; the requirement tests the notification's own email
status success kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy

requirements.text: for the customer whose active case Tabitha was handling, send a report notification
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE case_id = 1088
assumptions: case 1088 is canceled, so its customer (Cox, Foster and Gilmore, contact Patrick Ross) gets no new notification; it has one notification on the seed

notes:
No disagreements: the two independent passes agree on every requirement, value and disposition; their texts and assumptions differ in wording only.
The request speaks of 'the customer whose active case Tabitha was handling' in the singular, but Tabitha holds two active cases for two customers (251 for Vehement Capital Partners, 1142 for Hernandez, Barnett and Stewart), so each case's contact gets a report notification. 'Their contact' is read as the case's contact: for case 1142 that is David Trujillo, while the account's primary contact is Nathan Scott (contact 111); the request does not name the primary contact.
The benchmark's two notification checks join the case to its contact's user email but never test the notification's own recipient; the requirements carry each check and add the recipient address, which the request fixes ('to their contact'). The notification's message (new owner assigned, now managed by Case Assignment_3) has no column in the notification table, so it is not testable.
'Offboard Tabitha Bullock from our frontline case queue' is read as the summary of the steps that follow (reassign her active cases, then deactivate her profile); removing her membership of group 67 (Account Management_4) is not asked for in so many words and no listed tool removes a membership, so it is not a requirement. The order 'after the reassignment is complete' cannot be seen in the final state.
The acting user, Jose Roberson (user 32), is an admin but inactive on the seed; the policy has the assistant act with admin rights by default and states no bar on an inactive acting user.
